take_homes: Start from my teammate's job and pick the sharing shape against it. Don't start from what I built or what platform we have.
The agent file doesn't travel. The memory, the corrections and a named person who answers for the output are what make it work, and the owner is the part that doesn't copy.
An empty owner field in the people plan is the real finding. I need one name and one conversation before I build more.

monday.move: Pick one teammate on the pricing working group, ask how she does the pilot-cohort brief today, and test one switch assumption: that she'd use my brief if it landed in the working group's shared channel. Also ask who in the team owns the shared context files.
monday.who: One of my fourteen, probably the analyst who builds the pilot-cohort numbers. The owner question goes to my own leadership group.
monday.when: Monday morning, a 20-minute conversation, before I rerun the brief with fresh data.
monday.stop_condition: She says she'd still rebuild it herself, or nobody takes the owner role. Then I treat that as the finding and don't build the shared version.
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the context files, and everyone keeps their own copy. Nobody owns it yet.

misconception.why: The module never talks about prompts. It puts the value in curated context, corrections and an owner. That undercuts 'better prompts', though I still think prompt quality matters for my own work.

one_line: Less about AI than about why good things don't get picked up in a company. The pricing case and the empty owner fields are worth the hour, and the middle repeats itself.
